products.overview: A reactor, a pipeline, or a conveyor belt isn't a place for a delicate instrument. It's dusty, it swings in temperature, and it's often somewhere the safety rules don't let a standard analyzer sit at all. MATRIX-F II solves that with distance: the spectrometer sits in a protected analysis house, and an industry-hardened fiber optic probe reaches into the process itself, with no measurement delay. It's the only FT-NIR spectrometer that measures both in contact and contactless with one instrument, using fiber optic probes for direct immersion and fiber-coupled heads with tungsten sources for contactless measurement from a distance, up to six connected at once. Ten years of warranty cover the interferometer and the solid-state laser, and Bruker states thousands of these are already installed across chemical, pharmaceutical, and food manufacturing.
features: Contact and Contactless in One Instrument: Fiber optic probes for direct immersion, or tungsten-illuminated heads for remote measurement, on the same platform.
Up to Six Contactless Heads: Connects simultaneously to one MATRIX-F II emission or duplex spectrometer for multi-point monitoring.
Four Configuration Variants: Classical, emission, duplex, or ATEX-rated exproof, matched to your installation.
10-Year Warranty: Covers the interferometer's moving parts and the solid-state laser.
Direct Method Transfer: Develop a method in the lab, then move the same instrument straight into the process application.
User-Exchangeable Consumables: Sit on pre-aligned mounts, replaceable without realigning the optics.
Built-In Validation: An automated filter wheel and the OPUS Validation Program confirm in-spec performance, required for pharmaceutical use.
Industry-Standard Connectivity: CMET software and OPC support 4-20mA, Modbus, and Profibus DP, for integration into any existing control system.
Rugged, Low-Maintenance Design: A long-life NIR source and solid-state laser diode reduce service visits and cost of ownership.

faqs.question: What is the MATRIX-F II FT-NIR Process Spectrometer used for?
faqs.answer: MATRIX-F II is used for direct, real-time monitoring of chemical processes in reactors, pipelines, and conveyor belts, across chemical, pharmaceutical, and food manufacturing.

faqs.question: What makes MATRIX-F II different from a standard FT-NIR spectrometer?
faqs.answer: It's the only FT-NIR spectrometer that measures both in contact and contactless with one instrument, using fiber optic probes for direct measurement and fiber-coupled heads for remote measurement.

faqs.question: How do I choose between contact and contactless measurement for my process?
faqs.answer: Use a fiber optic probe wherever direct immersion into the process is possible, and a contactless head where physical contact isn't practical, such as a moving conveyor belt or web; the duplex variant supports both at once.

faqs.question: How do I set up monitoring for multiple points on one production line?
faqs.answer: Connect up to six contactless heads to a single MATRIX-F II emission or duplex spectrometer, allowing simultaneous monitoring across multiple points from one instrument.

faqs.question: Can MATRIX-F II be installed in a hazardous or ATEX-classified area?
faqs.answer: Yes, using the MATRIX-F exproof variant, certified to II 2G Ex px II T6 Gb and II (1) G [Ex op is T4 Ga] II C standards.

faqs.question: Can a method developed in the lab be used directly in the process?
faqs.answer: Yes. MATRIX-F II can run as a stand-alone laboratory system during method development, then transfer directly into the process application without redevelopment.

faqs.question: What is the warranty on the MATRIX-F II?
faqs.answer: 10 years on the interferometer's moving parts and the solid-state laser.

faqs.question: Is MATRIX-F II suitable for pharmaceutical manufacturing?
faqs.answer: Yes. An automated filter wheel and the OPUS Validation Program confirm the instrument operates within specification, which Bruker states is the precondition for pharmaceutical applications.

faqs.question: How does MATRIX-F II connect to existing plant control systems?
faqs.answer: Through CMET software with an OPC interface, supporting standard protocols including 4-20mA, Modbus, and Profibus DP.

longForm.heroLead: The spectrometer stays safe. The probe goes where the process is. A reactor, a pipeline, or a conveyor belt isn't a place for a delicate instrument. It's dusty, it swings in temperature, and it's often somewhere the safety rules don't let a standard analyzer sit at all. MATRIX-F II solves that with distance. The spectrometer sits in an analysis house, and an industry-hardened fiber optic probe reaches into the process itself, with no measurement delay. It's the only FT-NIR spectrometer that measures both in contact and contactless with one instrument. Fiber optic probes handle direct immersion measurements; fiber-coupled heads with tungsten sources handle contactless measurement from a distance, up to six connected at once. Ten years of warranty cover the interferometer and the solid-state laser. Bruker states thousands of these are already installed across chemical, pharmaceutical, and food manufacturing.

sections.title: MATRIX-F II FT-NIR Process Spectrometer at a Glance
sections.description: Everything you need to evaluate the MATRIX-F II: how contact and contactless measurement work together, which variant fits your installation, what applications it supports, and Inkarp installation and service support.
body: MATRIX-F II keeps the spectrometer in a protected location while fiber optic probes or contactless heads reach into the actual process, eliminating measurement delay without exposing the instrument.

One instrument, two measurement methods. Fiber optic probes handle direct contact measurement; contactless heads use tungsten illumination for remote measurement, and both can run together on the duplex variant.
Built for the environment you actually have. Free-standing NEMA 5/IP65 housing, 19-inch rack mounting, or a fully ATEX-rated exproof variant for hazardous zones.
A method developed in the lab moves straight to the plant. MATRIX-F II can run as a stand-alone lab system during method development, then move into the process application directly.
Maintenance doesn't mean downtime. Consumables sit on pre-aligned, user-exchangeable mounts, with no realignment needed after replacement.

Validation is built for regulated industries. An automated filter wheel and the OPUS Validation Program confirm the instrument is operating within specification, the stated precondition for pharmaceutical use.
It plugs into whatever control system you're already running. CMET software and OPC support standard protocols including 4-20mA, Modbus, and Profibus DP.

Confirmed solution: Bruker MATRIX-F II FT-NIR Process Spectrometer. Four variants: classical (probes and flow cells), emission (contactless heads only), duplex (both simultaneously), exproof (ATEX-rated). Warranty: 10 years, interferometer moving parts and solid-state laser. Full performance specifications (spectral range, resolution, dimensions, weight, power) are available on request from Inkarp.

sections.eyebrow: Fiber Optic Probes and Contactless Measurement
sections.title: Choosing probes, heads, or both
body: Choosing between contact and contactless measurement, or using both, comes down to what your process point actually allows.

Fiber optic probes go into the process directly, as diffuse reflectance, transflectance, or transmission probes, in materials like stainless steel or Hastelloy, or as flow cells for pilot plant assemblies. Contactless heads use tungsten illumination to measure from a distance, with the scattered light carried back to the spectrometer by fiber, useful where physical contact with the process isn't practical or safe. The duplex variant runs both at once, so a single instrument covers a reactor immersion probe and a remote conveyor head simultaneously.
